title: Runtime validation vs compile-time types
description: Understand the difference between compile-time types and runtime validation, and when to use each in a React application.

data.text: TypeScript checks types at compile time, but JavaScript runs at runtime. The gap between these two worlds is where many bugs hide. Understanding when compile-time types are enough, and when you need runtime validation, is essential for trustworthy React applications.

TypeScript interfaces and type aliases catch errors while you write code. They are excellent for component props, state shapes, function arguments, and internal data flow. But once the code compiles, those types are erased. They do not exist at runtime.

data.title: Compile-Time Safety Only

data.text: Runtime validation checks the actual shape of data when it enters your application. This is critical for API responses, form submissions, URL parameters, and any data from external sources. A validation library can throw an error or return a result type that tells you whether the data is valid.

data.title: Validating an API Response
data.content: Using a schema to validate incoming data

cards.title: Compile-Time Types
cards.description: Check shapes while you write code. Types are removed when JavaScript runs.

cards.title: Runtime Validation
cards.description: Check actual data when it arrives. Runs in the browser or server.
pros: Works at the boundary of your system

data.text: A good rule of thumb is to use compile-time types for everything inside your application and runtime validation at every boundary. A boundary is anywhere external data crosses into your system: API responses, form submissions, cookies, localStorage, and WebSocket messages.

data.title: Trust but Verify
data.text: TypeScript types are a promise you make to other developers. Runtime validation is a promise you enforce for external data. Use both together for the safest architecture.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Compile-time types are erased at runtime
Runtime validation protects external data at system boundaries
Use both: types inside, validation at the edges
Validate API responses, form data, and environment variables
data.takeaway: Types make development safer; runtime validation makes production safer.
